name: Twist
tagline: Host asynchronous team threads organized by channel and topic

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 1 month of message history; 5 integrations; 5 GB storage; up to 500 internal members and 500 external guests

tiers.name: Unlimited
tiers.limits: Unlimited message history, integrations and storage; up to 500 internal members and 500 external guests

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 month of history; 5 integrations; 5 GB storage; up to 500 internal members plus 500 external guests
pricing.hiddenCosts: All internal team members and multi-channel guests are billable on Unlimited; single-channel guests are free. New users are prorated and removals create account credit after the refund window; a workspace cannot mix Free and Unlimited members.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Twist, host asynchronous team threads organized by channel and topic. The hard boundary is cross-platform apps, notifications, email integration, search, and doist reliability, plus network, moderation, and communication infrastructure.
coreLoopDIY: Host a private space for asynchronous team threads, organize discussion into channels and topics, and keep membership and moderation under the owner's control.
whatYouLose: cross-platform apps, notifications, email integration, search, and Doist reliability
ongoingBurden: realtime delivery, notifications, abuse handling, search, media, permissions, mobile clients, backups, and community operations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Twist because community software is valuable when members are already there and the operator does not have to own realtime reliability and abuse response. The recurring cost buys realtime delivery, notifications, abuse handling, search, media, permissions, mobile clients, backups, and community operations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Discourse
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source community discussion platform with strong moderation and search.

alternatives.name: Discourse
alternatives.desc: Long-lived topic threads with search and notifications; more public-forum-shaped than workplace-shaped.

facts.install: Use the official Docker installer on a 64-bit Linux server; managed Discourse hosting is the paid alternative
facts.dataFormat: Persistent records in PostgreSQL, Redis for cache/queues, and uploads/backups/logs in the Docker volume or S3-compatible storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Discourse is public-forum shaped and lacks Twist's workplace-native channel organization, calm team onboarding and managed integrations.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs a Linux VPS, Docker, DNS, TLS, working SMTP and regular upgrades

alternatives.name: Mattermost Team Edition
alternatives.desc: Channels and threads work, but Mattermost still rewards live chat more than Twist's deliberate silence.

facts.install: Deploy the official Linux Docker Compose stack or install the compiled server binary with PostgreSQL
facts.dataFormat: Messages and metadata in PostgreSQL; uploaded files in the server data directory or configured S3-compatible storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Mattermost remains live-chat-first rather than deliberately async, and the current free edition's message-history visibility limit weakens it as a long-term searchable archive.
facts.setupBlocker: A Linux server, Docker/PostgreSQL, DNS, TLS and SMTP are required; current free Team Edition also limits long-term message-history visibility

alternatives.name: Pumble Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited threaded history for free; topic structure is looser, so humans must supply the discipline.

facts.install: Hosted signup, with optional desktop and mobile apps
facts.dataFormat: Messages, channels and files in Pumble's managed cloud; the free workspace includes 10 GB of shared storage and supports workspace export
facts.gapVsPaid: Pumble has channels and threads but no strong topic taxonomy, so teams must enforce the organization that Twist builds into every conversation.

alternatives.name: Zulip
alternatives.desc: The closest free answer: streams hold channels, topics hold threads, and every reply lands somewhere deliberate.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or run the official install script/Docker deployment on supported Ubuntu or Debian
facts.dataFormat: Persistent messages and organization data in PostgreSQL; uploads locally or in S3-compatible storage; exports are tar.gz archives containing JSON and files
facts.gapVsPaid: Zulip is the closest structural match, but its free cloud search stops at 10,000 messages and self-hosting replaces Twist's managed operations with a Linux service.
facts.setupBlocker: Free cloud search stops at 10,000 messages; self-hosting needs a Linux VM, DNS/TLS, outgoing email and at least about 2 GB RAM

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Unlimited plan and a single private community DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Twist in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, WebSockets, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: host a private space for asynchronous team threads, organize discussion into channels and topics, and keep membership and moderation under the owner's control.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement spaces, channels, topics, replies, reactions, mentions, profiles, roles, and invitations.
Use WebSockets for live updates but preserve every message transactionally in PostgreSQL.
Add moderation queues, reports, blocks, rate limits, attachment limits, and an audit log.
Provide email digests, browser notifications, search, pinned content, and member export.
Add owner-controlled retention, account deletion, backup, restore, and health checks.
Ship Docker Compose with a seeded demo, migrations, and an emergency admin command.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out public-network discovery and existing member liquidity.
Deliberately leave out production voice or video rooms.
Deliberately leave out native mobile applications, enterprise SSO, and 24-hour abuse operations.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
